subs.name: 二氧化硅（石英砂）
subs.note: 原料，来源是沙子与石英。
subs.noteEn: The feedstock, from sand and quartz.

subs.name: 焦炭
subs.note: 还原剂，自己被氧化成 CO。
subs.noteEn: Reducer; itself oxidized to CO.

subs.name: 硅（粗硅 → 高纯硅）
subs.note: 第一步只得 98~99% 粗硅，第三步才沉积出高纯硅。
subs.noteEn: Step one gives only 98–99% crude; step three deposits pure Si.

subs.name: 一氧化碳
subs.note: 电弧炉尾气，可燃、有毒。
subs.noteEn: Toxic, flammable off-gas of the furnace.

subs.name: 氯化氢
subs.note: 第二步消耗、第三步再生，可循环利用。
subs.noteEn: Used in step two, regenerated in step three; recycled.

subs.name: 三氯氢硅
subs.note: 液态中间体，蒸馏即可除去硼、磷等杂质。
subs.noteEn: Liquid intermediate; distillation strips boron and phosphorus.

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 还原剂，把硅从 SiHCl₃ 里重新放出来。
subs.noteEn: Reducer that frees silicon again from SiHCl₃.

term: 粗硅提纯与半导体级硅
oneLiner: 石英砂用焦炭还原得粗硅，转成三氯氢硅蒸馏后再氢还原，区熔得 9N 高纯硅。
oneLinerEn: Coke reduces quartz to crude Si; convert it to SiHCl₃, distill, reduce with H₂, then zone-refine to 9N.
detail: 三步提纯：石英砂与焦炭在电弧炉约 2000 ℃ 还原得冶金级粗硅；粗硅与 HCl 在铜催化下生成液态的三氯氢硅，蒸馏除去硼、磷等杂质；再用氢气在高温下还原，硅沉积在硅芯上，经区熔或直拉法制成单晶硅锭，纯度可达 99.9999999%（9N）。芯片用硅要求极高，因为痕量的硼、磷就会显著改变导电性——这也是废旧芯片值得回收提金的前提。首步其实是碳从二氧化硅中夺氧的还原——SiO₂ + 2C 在高温下生成 Si 与 CO↑，硅的氧化数由 +4 降到 0，是典型的「氧化还原反应」。
detailEn: Three steps: quartz sand plus coke in an arc furnace near 2000 °C gives metallurgical-grade silicon; it reacts with HCl over a copper catalyst to form liquid trichlorosilane, which is distilled to strip boron and phosphorus; hydrogen then reduces it back to silicon deposited on seeds, and zone refining or the Czochralski pull yields an ingot up to 99.9999999% (9N). Chip-grade silicon must be that pure because traces of boron or phosphorus already shift conductivity — which is exactly why scrap chips are worth reprocessing. The first step is really carbon stripping oxygen from silica: SiO₂ + 2C gives Si + CO↑ at furnace heat, with silicon dropping from +4 to 0 — a textbook redox (see Redox).

subs.name: 硫铁矿（黄铁矿）
subs.note: 廉价硫源，在沸腾炉中焙烧。
subs.noteEn: Cheap sulfur source, roasted in a fluidized bed.

subs.name: 氧气（空气）
subs.note: 两步都要用空气提供。
subs.noteEn: Supplied as air in two of the steps.

subs.name: 氧化铁（炉渣）
subs.note: 炉渣可返作炼铁原料或制水泥。
subs.noteEn: Slag goes back to ironmaking or cement.

subs.name: 二氧化硫
subs.note: 中间产物，也是酸雨主因，尾气须回收。
subs.noteEn: Intermediate; also the acid-rain gas, so off-gas is scrubbed.

subs.name: 三氧化硫
subs.note: 催化氧化的产物，不能直接用水吸收。
subs.noteEn: From catalytic oxidation; must not be absorbed by water directly.

subs.name: 五氧化二钒（催化剂）
subs.note: 加快平衡到达，不改变平衡位置。
subs.noteEn: Speeds up reaching equilibrium; shifts nothing.

subs.name: 发烟硫酸
subs.note: SO₃ 溶于 98.3% 浓硫酸的产物。
subs.noteEn: SO₃ dissolved in 98.3% sulfuric acid.

subs.name: 硫酸
subs.note: 既是吸收剂又是最终产品，稀释后出厂。
subs.noteEn: Both absorbent and final product, diluted before shipping.

oneLiner: 焙烧得 SO₂，V₂O₅ 催化氧化成 SO₃，再用 98.3% 浓硫酸吸收后稀释。
oneLinerEn: Roast to SO₂, oxidize over V₂O₅ to SO₃, absorb in 98.3% acid, then dilute.
detail: 三步：焙烧、催化氧化、吸收。SO₂ 氧化为 SO₃ 时气体分子数减小且放热，理论上低温加压有利，但低温下 V₂O₅ 活性不足，所以取 400~500 ℃、常压这个折中点。SO₃ 不直接溶于水，否则形成雾状硫酸难以沉降且腐蚀设备，工业用 98.3% 浓硫酸吸收。硫酸的产量长期被当作工业化的指标：化肥、石油精炼、冶金、蓄电池、洗涤剂全部依赖它。尾气中的 SO₂ 用氨法吸收制取硫酸铵，既省原料又防酸雨。
detailEn: Three stages: roasting, catalytic oxidation, absorption. Oxidizing SO₂ shrinks gas volume and gives off heat, so low temperature and high pressure favour it in theory — but V₂O₅ is inactive when cold, so plants compromise at 400–500 °C and near ambient pressure. SO₃ is never absorbed in water directly, which would make a mist of sulfuric acid that will not settle and eats the equipment; 98.3% acid does the absorbing. Sulfuric acid output has long been read as a proxy for industrialization: fertilizer, refining, metallurgy, batteries and detergents all depend on it. Off-gas SO₂ is scrubbed with ammonia to give ammonium sulfate, saving feedstock and preventing acid rain.

subs.name: 氨
subs.note: 由合成氨装置直接供料，两大工艺链相接。
subs.noteEn: Fed straight from the ammonia plant; two process chains meet.

subs.name: 氧气（过量空气）
subs.note: 氧化剂，吸收塔还要再通一次。
subs.noteEn: Oxidizer; passed in again in the absorber.

subs.name: 铂铑合金网（催化剂）
subs.note: 极贵且易中砷、铅中毒，需净制原料气。
subs.noteEn: Costly and easily poisoned by arsenic or lead; gas must be cleaned.

subs.name: 一氧化氮
subs.note: 无色，出装置即变红棕；水中吸收时又会逸出循环。
subs.noteEn: Colourless, browns on escape; recirculates from the water absorption.

subs.name: 二氧化氮
subs.note: 红棕色有毒气体，被水与氧吸收成酸。
subs.noteEn: Red-brown toxic gas, absorbed by water and oxygen into acid.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 吸收塔的液相，也是副产蒸汽的来源。
subs.noteEn: The absorber's liquid phase; also raises steam from the heat.

subs.name: 硝酸
subs.note: 产品，约 50~68%，可再浓缩。
subs.noteEn: Product, about 50–68%; can be concentrated further.

oneLiner: 氨在铂铑网上催化氧化成 NO，再氧化为 NO₂，在过量空气下用水吸收成硝酸。
oneLinerEn: Ammonia burns to NO over Pt-Rh gauze, oxidizes to NO₂, and is absorbed with excess air into nitric acid.
detail: 奥斯特瓦尔德法。氨氧化在约 800 ℃ 的铂铑网上瞬时完成且放热，反应热可维持自身温度，但必须防止砷、铅使催化剂中毒。NO 遇空气即变红棕色 NO₂；用水吸收时每 3 个 NO₂ 只有 2 个成酸、另 1 个回到 NO，所以工业上在吸收塔里大量通空气把 NO 反复氧化吸收，总结果相当于第四式。主要用途是硝酸铵与硝基化肥、炸药，以及尼龙的中间体己二酸；浓硝酸还用于金属钝化与蚀刻。尾气中的 NOx 用碱液或催化还原除去。
detailEn: The Ostwald process. Ammonia oxidation runs instantaneously on Pt-Rh gauze at about 800 °C and gives off enough heat to sustain itself, but arsenic and lead must be kept out or the catalyst dies. NO browns to NO₂ in air; water absorption turns only 2 of every 3 NO₂ into acid and sends 1 back to NO, so plants flood the absorber with air to re-oxidize and re-absorb it, which is what the fourth line summarizes. Uses: ammonium nitrate and nitrogen fertilizer, explosives, adipic acid for nylon; concentrated acid also passivates and etches metals. Tail-gas NOx is removed with alkali or catalytic reduction.

subs.name: 氧化铝（自铝土矿提纯）
subs.note: 原料，需先用氢氧化钠溶出重结晶（拜耳法）。
subs.noteEn: Feedstock, first dissolved in NaOH and recrystallized (Bayer process).

subs.name: 冰晶石（熔剂）
subs.note: 把电解温度从 2050 ℃ 降到约 960 ℃。
subs.noteEn: Drops the operating temperature from 2050 °C to about 960 °C.

subs.name: 碳素阳极
subs.note: 参与反应被消耗，需定期更换。
subs.noteEn: Consumed by the oxygen it meets; replaced regularly.

subs.name: 铝液
subs.note: 密度大于电解质，沉在槽底定期抽出。
subs.noteEn: Denser than the bath, so it pools at the bottom and is tapped.

subs.name: 氧气
subs.note: 阳极产物，随即与碳块反应。
subs.noteEn: Anode product, which attacks the carbon immediately.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 阳极消耗的真实产物，也是碳排放主项。
subs.noteEn: The real anode output, and the plant's main emission.

oneLiner: 氧化铝溶进熔融冰晶石，在 960 ℃ 电解即可得铝，远低于直接熔化所需的 2050 ℃。
oneLinerEn: Alumina dissolved in molten cryolite electrolyzes at 960 °C — far below its 2050 °C melting point.
detail: 氧化铝熔点高达 2050 ℃，直接熔化电解既耗能又损毁内衬；溶入冰晶石 Na₃AlF₆ 后在 950~980 ℃ 就能通电分解，这是 Hall–Héroult 法的核心。阳极产生的氧会把碳块烧成 CO₂，所以阳极要不断补充，电耗与阳极材料占了成本大头——而回收一吨再生铝只需原铝约 5% 的能量。上游的拜耳法用浓 NaOH 溶出铝土矿中的 Al₂O₃，杂质作为红色赤泥排出，堆存是铝工业的主要环境负担。
detailEn: Alumina melts at 2050 °C, too hot to electrolyze directly without wrecking the lining; dissolved in cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) it breaks down at 950–980 °C, which is the core of the Hall–Héroult process. The oxygen liberated burns the carbon anode to CO₂, so anodes are eaten away and must be replaced — power and anodes dominate the cost, which is why recycling a tonne of aluminum takes only about 5% of the energy of primary metal. Upstream, the Bayer process leaches the ore with concentrated NaOH and discards the impurities as red mud, the industry's main waste burden.

subs.name: 粗铜（作阳极）
subs.note: 火法炼出的约 99%，含 Fe、Zn、Ni、Au、Ag 等杂质。
subs.noteEn: About 99% from smelting, holding Fe, Zn, Ni, Au and Ag.

subs.name: 铜离子（电解液）
subs.note: 阳极溶入、阴极析出，溶液浓度基本不变。
subs.noteEn: Enters at the anode, leaves at the cathode; strength stays steady.

subs.name: 电子（外电路）
subs.note: 阳极失电子溶解，阴极得电子析出。
subs.noteEn: Given up as the anode dissolves, taken up as copper plates out.

subs.name: 电解铜（阴极析出，99.95%+）
subs.note: 纯度达 99.95% 以上，导电用铜必须到这个级别。
subs.noteEn: 99.95%+; conducting copper has to reach this grade.

subs.name: 锌离子（进入溶液）
subs.note: 比铜活泼的杂质同溶但不析出，靠电位控制。
subs.noteEn: More active impurities dissolve but will not plate out at this potential.

subs.name: 阳极泥（金、银与铂族）
subs.note: 比铜惰性的金属不溶解，脱落沉入槽底。
subs.noteEn: Metals less active than copper never dissolve; they drop to the cell bottom.

term: 铜的电解精炼与阳极泥
termEn: Electrorefining Copper and the Anode Slime
oneLiner: 粗铜作阳极溶解、纯铜在阴极析出，不溶的金银铂族沉入槽底成为阳极泥。
oneLinerEn: The anode dissolves and pure copper plates out; insoluble Au, Ag and PGMs fall as anode slime.
detail: 火法炼出的铜约 99%，而导电用铜要求 99.95% 以上，靠电解精炼完成：粗铜作阳极、纯铜片作阴极、硫酸酸化的 CuSO₄ 溶液作电解液。通电后阳极上的铜溶解，在阴极按电位控制重新析出，比铜活泼的 Fe、Zn、Ni 虽一同进入溶液却不达析出电位，留在液里；比铜惰性的金、银和铂族金属根本不能溶解，只能从阳极脱落沉底，这就是阳极泥。它是冶炼厂提炼金银与铂族元素的主要原料，也是重要副产品收入。与电子废弃物提金相比，阳极泥里的金是火法富集的“顺带”产物，品位高且无需王水。
detailEn: Smelted copper is about 99% pure, but conducting copper needs 99.95%+, so it is electrorefined: blister copper as anode, a pure-copper sheet as cathode, acidified CuSO₄ solution as electrolyte. Copper dissolves off the anode and plates back under potential control; more active Fe, Zn and Ni enter the solution but never reach their deposition potential and stay there, while gold, silver and the platinum group cannot dissolve at all — they simply fall from the anode as slime. That slime is the chief feedstock for refining precious metals and a major by-product credit for the smelter. Unlike e-waste gold recovery, the gold in anode slime has already been concentrated by fire, at high grade and with no aqua regia involved.

subs.name: 氯气（氧化剂）
subs.note: 活泼性 Br₂ < Cl₂，所以氯能把溴置换出来。
subs.noteEn: Chlorine is the stronger oxidizer, so it displaces bromine.

subs.name: 溴离子（苦卤中）
subs.note: 海水中约 65 mg/L，晒盐母液被浓缩一个量级以上。
subs.noteEn: About 65 mg/L in seawater, over ten times richer in the salt-pan mother liquor.

subs.name: 溴单质
subs.note: 唯一常温下为液态的非金属单质，易挥发、强腐蚀。
subs.noteEn: The only liquid nonmetal at room temperature; volatile and corrosive.

subs.name: 氯离子
subs.note: 氯气被还原后的产物，留在卤水中。
subs.noteEn: What chlorine becomes; stays in the liquor.

subs.name: 二氧化硫（吸收剂）
subs.note: 把吹出的 Br₂ 还原成 HBr 溶于水，实现富集。
subs.noteEn: Reduces the blown-out Br₂ to soluble HBr, concentrating it.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 吸收塔的溶剂，也参与反应。
subs.noteEn: The absorbing medium and a reactant.

subs.name: 氢溴酸
subs.note: 富集后的中间形态，再氯化即得高纯溴。
subs.noteEn: The concentrated intermediate; re-chlorination yields pure bromine.

subs.name: 硫酸
subs.note: SO₂ 被溴氧化的产物。
subs.noteEn: What SO₂ is oxidized to during absorption.

subs.name: 盐酸
subs.note: 再氯化时的副产酸，可回用于酸化。
subs.noteEn: By-product acid, reusable for acidifying the feed.

oneLiner: 氯气氧化苦卤中的溴离子，热空气吹出溴，SO₂ 吸收富集后再氯化。
oneLinerEn: Chlorinate bromide in bittern, blow the bromine out with air, absorb it in SO₂ to concentrate, then chlorinate again.
detail: 海水中溴只有约 65 mg/L，直接提取不划算；工业上取晒盐后的苦卤，先酸化再通氯把 Br⁻ 氧化成 Br₂，用热空气或水蒸气把 Br₂ 吹出，以 SO₂ 水溶液吸收转成 HBr 富集，最后再氯化得到商品溴。整套氧化—吹出—吸收—再氧化的本质是反复浓缩。溴主要用于阻燃剂、感光材料 AgBr、医药与农药，也用作油田完井液 CaBr₂。氯能把溴从其盐里置换出来（Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ 生成 2Cl⁻ + Br₂），靠的是氯的氧化性强于溴，正落在「氧化还原反应」的强弱判据里。
detailEn: Seawater holds only about 65 mg/L of bromine — too dilute to work on directly. Industry takes the bittern left after solar salt: acidify, chlorinate the Br⁻ to Br₂, strip the bromine out with hot air or steam, absorb it in aqueous SO₂ to concentrate it as HBr, then chlorinate once more to sellable bromine. The whole oxidize–blow-out–absorb–re-oxidize loop is repeated concentration. Bromine goes mainly into flame retardants, photographic AgBr, pharmaceuticals and pesticides, plus calcium bromide completion fluids in oil wells. Chlorine displaces bromine from its salts (Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ gives 2Cl⁻ + Br₂) because chlorine is the stronger oxidizer, the very strength ranking behind redox (see Redox).

<svg viewBox="0 0 360 190" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="sans-serif">

subs.name: 石灰石（或贝壳）
subs.note: 煅烧后提供沉淀剂，海边贝壳就是现成原料。
subs.noteEn: Calcined to give the precipitant; seashells serve as the feedstock.

subs.name: 生石灰
subs.note: 消化成石灰乳后使用。
subs.noteEn: Slaked to milk of lime before dosing.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 煅烧石灰石的副产气。
subs.noteEn: Off-gas from calcining the limestone.

subs.name: 氯化镁（苦卤中）
subs.note: 海水蒸发浓缩后的镁存留形态，海水中镁约 1.3 g/L。
subs.noteEn: How the magnesium sits once seawater is concentrated; about 1.3 g/L in the sea.

subs.name: 石灰乳
subs.note: 廉价碱，把镁沉淀下来而不引入新杂质。
subs.noteEn: A cheap base that drops the magnesium without new impurities.

subs.name: 氢氧化镁沉淀
subs.note: 溶解度极小，是富集镁的关键一步。
subs.noteEn: Barely soluble — the concentration step.

subs.name: 氯化钙
subs.note: 滤液成分，可作融雪剂与干燥剂。
subs.noteEn: Stays in the filtrate; useful as de-icer and desiccant.

subs.name: 盐酸
subs.note: 把沉淀重新溶解为氯化镁。
subs.noteEn: Redissolves the precipitate as the chloride.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 中和产物；脱水环节必须在 HCl 气氛中抑制水解。
subs.noteEn: Neutralization product; drying must run in HCl to stop hydrolysis.

subs.name: 金属镁
subs.note: 轻合金与烟花照明弹的原料，燃烧发耀眼白光。
subs.noteEn: For light alloys and flares; burns with a dazzling white flame.

subs.name: 氯气（副产）
subs.note: 电解副产，回收后用于制盐酸循环使用。
subs.noteEn: Recovered from the cell and burned back into the HCl loop.

term: 海水提镁（沉淀—酸化—电解）
oneLiner: 石灰乳把苦卤中的镁沉淀为 Mg(OH)₂，盐酸溶解后电解熔融氯化镁。
oneLinerEn: Precipitate magnesium as hydroxide with milk of lime, redissolve in HCl, then electrolyze the molten chloride.
detail: 镁是海水中第二多的金属离子，约 1.3 g/L。工艺先煅烧石灰石或贝壳得到 CaO，消化成石灰乳加入苦卤，生成溶解度极小的 Mg(OH)₂；过滤后用盐酸溶解、蒸发结晶，再在 HCl 气氛中脱水得到无水氯化镁，最后电解熔融盐制得金属镁。注意：直接加热 MgCl₂·6H₂O 会因水解而得到 MgO，拿不到无水盐。镁合金轻而强度高，用于航空与汽车；MgO 是优质耐火材料。镁很活泼，只能靠电解熔融 MgCl₂ 冶炼、无法从水溶液里电积出来，这与钠、铝同走电解熔盐一路（见「金属活动性顺序」）。
detailEn: Magnesium is the second most abundant metal ion in seawater, about 1.3 g/L. The route calcines limestone or shells to CaO, slakes it into milk of lime and drops nearly insoluble Mg(OH)₂ from the bittern; the solid is redissolved in hydrochloric acid, evaporated, then dried in an HCl atmosphere to give anhydrous MgCl₂, which is electrolyzed as a melt. The catch: heating MgCl₂·6H₂O outright just hydrolyses it to MgO. Magnesium alloys are light and strong for aircraft and cars, and MgO is a top-grade refractory. Magnesium is reactive enough that it must be won by electrolysing molten MgCl₂ and cannot be plated from solution, the same molten-salt route as sodium and aluminium (see The Reactivity Series of Metals).

subs.name: 十六烷（重油代表物）
subs.note: 沸点高、不能直接当汽油用的长链烷烃。
subs.noteEn: A long-chain alkane too high-boiling to go straight into petrol.

subs.name: 辛烷（汽油组分）
subs.note: 裂化的目标产物；其异构体异辛烷定辛烷值为 100。
subs.noteEn: The target of cracking; its isomer is set at octane number 100.

subs.name: 辛烯
subs.note: 裂化同时生成的烯烃，含它越多裂化汽油越易氧化变质。
subs.noteEn: The alkene co-product; more of it makes cracked gasoline age faster.

subs.name: 乙烷
subs.note: 天然气与炼厂气的主要成分，裂解最便宜的原料。
subs.noteEn: From natural gas and refinery gas — the cheapest cracker feed.

subs.name: 乙烯
subs.note: 产量常被视为衡量石油化工发展水平的标志。
subs.noteEn: Its output is a standing yardstick of a country's petrochemical industry.

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 裂解副产，也大量用于炼油加氢。
subs.noteEn: A cracker by-product, and a major refinery consumable.

subs.name: 氧气（空气）
subs.note: 燃烧必需；供不足则生成有毒的 CO。
subs.noteEn: Needed to burn; short supply yields toxic CO.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 完全燃烧的产物，交通排放的主要碳源。
subs.noteEn: Product of complete combustion and the main transport-related carbon output.

subs.name: 水（蒸气）
subs.note: 氢的去处，以水蒸气形式随烟气排出。
subs.noteEn: Where the hydrogen ends up, leaving with the flue gas as vapor.

term: 石油的分馏、裂化与裂解
oneLiner: 分馏按沸点切割是物理变化，裂化与裂解把长链烃断开才是化学变化。
oneLinerEn: Fractionation sorts by boiling point — a physical change; cracking and pyrolysis break long chains, a chemical one.
detail: 石油是烷烃、环烷烃与芳香烃的混合物，分馏塔按沸点区间切出汽油、煤油、柴油与重油——分子本身没变，所以是物理变化。重油太多而汽油不够时就要裂化，把长链断短以提高汽油产率；再升温到 700 ℃ 以上就是裂解，目的是拿乙烯、丙烯这些化工原料。汽油标号指的是辛烷值：异辛烷抗爆好定为 100，正庚烷易爆震定为 0。各馏分本身仍是沸点相近的混合物；乙烯的产量常被当作一个国家石油化工发展水平的标志，它也是「有机化学基础」里聚合与众多衍生物的起点。
detailEn: Crude oil is a mixture of alkanes, cycloalkanes and aromatics; a fractionating column cuts it by boiling range into gasoline, kerosene, diesel and residue — the molecules are untouched, so this is a physical change. When the heavy end runs long and the gasoline end short, cracking breaks long chains short to lift gasoline yield; push the temperature past 700 °C and it is pyrolysis, aimed at ethylene and propylene as chemical feedstocks. Gasoline grades quote the octane number: isooctane, which resists knock, is set at 100 and heptane, which knocks badly, at 0. Each fraction is itself a mixture of nearby boiling points; ethylene output is often taken as a barometer of a country's petrochemical industry, and it is the starting point of polymerization and many derivatives in organic chemistry (see Organic Basics).

subs.name: 碳（焦炭/煤）
subs.note: 干馏后的残焦是气化的原料。
subs.noteEn: The coke left by carbonization feeds the gasifier.

subs.name: 水蒸气
subs.note: 与炽热焦炭反应，把氢送进合成气。
subs.noteEn: Meets the red-hot coke and carries the hydrogen in.

subs.name: 一氧化碳
subs.note: 合成气的一半；有毒，泄漏会致命。
subs.noteEn: Half of syngas; toxic, so leaks are lethal.

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 合成气的另一半，后续加氢反应的还原剂。
subs.noteEn: The other half, and the reductant for everything downstream.

subs.name: 甲醇
subs.note: 间接液化的产品，也可制烯烃与甲醛。
subs.noteEn: An indirect-liquefaction product, and a feed to olefins and formaldehyde.

subs.name: 甲烷（合成天然气）
subs.note: 甲烷化的产物，即煤制天然气。
subs.noteEn: The methanation product — coal-to-gas.

oneLiner: 隔绝空气高温干馏得焦炭与煤焦油，再气化成一氧化碳和氢气，合成甲醇或甲烷。
oneLinerEn: Heat coal without air for coke and tar, gasify the carbon to CO and H₂, then build methanol or methane.
detail: 干馏是隔绝空气加强热使煤分解，得到焦炭（冶金还原剂）、煤焦油（化工原料）、粗氨水与焦炉气（H₂、CH₄、CO、C₂H₄）——分子种类变了，与石油分馏的物理变化相对。气化把煤转成 CO 与 H₂ 的合成气，是整个煤化工的枢纽：合成气再制甲醇，或甲烷化制合成天然气。液化分直接液化（高温高压加氢）与间接液化（先气化再费托合成）。中国富煤、贫油、少气，煤制油与煤制气承担着一部分能源安全的考量。煤焦油经分馏可得苯、甲苯、二甲苯与酚、萘等芳香族原料，焦炉气里的 H₂ 与 CH₄ 则可作燃料或合成氨的原料气（见「工业合成氨」）。
detailEn: Carbonization heats coal without air until it decomposes, giving coke for smelting, coal tar for chemicals, weak aqueous ammonia, and coke-oven gas (H₂, CH₄, CO, C₂H₄) — the molecules themselves change, which is the point of contrast with physical fractionation of oil. Gasification converts coal to CO + H₂ syngas, the pivot of the whole industry: that syngas is then made into methanol or methanated to substitute natural gas. Liquefaction comes direct (hydrogen under heat and pressure) or indirect (gasify first, then Fischer–Tropsch). China's coal-rich, oil-poor, gas-lean balance is why coal-to-liquids and coal-to-gas carry an energy-security role here. Work-up of coal tar yields aromatic feedstocks such as benzene, toluene and phenol, while the H₂ and CH₄ in coke-oven gas serve as fuel or as synthesis gas for ammonia (see Ammonia Synthesis).

subs.name: 纯碱（苏打）
subs.note: 引入 Na₂O，作用是降低熔化温度。
subs.noteEn: Supplies Na₂O and lowers the melting temperature.

subs.name: 石英砂（二氧化硅）
subs.note: 玻璃网络的主体，也是陶瓷坯体的骨料。
subs.noteEn: The glass network former and the grit of the body.

subs.name: 硅酸钠
subs.note: 水玻璃的主成分，可溶、作胶粘剂。
subs.noteEn: The soluble 'water glass', used as a binder.

subs.name: 石灰石
subs.note: 玻璃里引入 CaO 提高耐水性；也是水泥的主要原料。
subs.noteEn: Supplies CaO for water resistance, and is the chief cement raw material.

subs.name: 硅酸钙
subs.note: 玻璃与水泥中都存在的骨架成分。
subs.noteEn: A structural constituent of both glass and cement.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 碳酸盐分解带出的气体，需在窑气中排出。
subs.noteEn: Gas driven off the carbonates and vented from the kiln.

subs.name: 高岭土（黏土主要成分）
subs.note: 陶瓷坯体的原料，带结构水。
subs.noteEn: The clay behind pottery; it carries structural water.

subs.name: 氧化铝
subs.note: 烧结后留在瓷体里，决定耐火与硬度。
subs.noteEn: Stays in the fired body, giving refractoriness and hardness.

subs.name: 结构水（蒸气）
subs.note: 必须缓慢升温排出，否则坯体开裂。
subs.noteEn: Must be driven off slowly or the ware cracks.

oneLiner: 纯碱、石灰石与石英砂高温成玻璃，石灰石加黏土煅烧成水泥，黏土烧结成陶瓷。
oneLinerEn: Soda, limestone and silica make glass; limestone with clay makes cement; fired clay makes ceramics.
detail: 这三样统称硅酸盐工业。普通玻璃用纯碱、石灰石与石英砂，高温下生成 Na₂SiO₃ 与 CaSiO₃，冷却后得到组成近似写作 Na₂O·CaO·6SiO₂ 的混合物；玻璃是非晶体，没有固定熔点，只有一段逐渐软化的温度区间。水泥用石灰石与黏土磨细煅烧，是水硬性胶凝材料——遇水反应硬化，所以受潮即废。陶瓷以黏土成型烧结，烧结时高岭土失去结构水。玻璃不在「晶体类型」的任何一格，正因非晶体而只有软化区间；把普通玻璃加热到近软化后骤冷即得钢化玻璃，表面形成的压让它更耐冲击、碎裂时也不生锐角。
detailEn: These three make up the silicate industry. Ordinary glass takes soda ash, limestone and quartz sand; at furnace heat they form Na₂SiO₃ and CaSiO₃, and the cooled product is a mixture written roughly as Na₂O·CaO·6SiO₂. Glass is amorphous — no fixed melting point, only a softening range. Cement is ground limestone and clay, calcined together; it sets hydraulically, reacting with water, so damp storage ruins it. Ceramics are shaped from clay and fired, the kaolinite giving up its structural water as it goes. Glass fits none of the crystal types, and being amorphous it has only a softening range; chilling glass heated near that point gives toughened glass, whose surface compression makes it far more impact-resistant and free of sharp shards (see Crystal Types).
